requirements: Passed current-source core report for the exact runtime, browser and Flashwright driver
Pinned isolated competitor dependencies and matching ChromeDriver/Cypress bundle
Separate current-source library admission before sampling; recheck every sample outcome
One-worker complete work including preparation and cleanup
Rotated engine order; no shared-host timing until coordinated
plan.limitation: Outcome admission does not establish equivalent work for Puppeteer, Cypress or WebdriverIO; no ranking is emitted by this harness.

acceptance.rationale: Require at least a 10% complete-flow improvement with a launch-clustered confidence interval excluding parity. Reject median regressions above 5%, observed tail regressions above 15%, and memory growth above 10% unless explicitly reviewed. Baseline-only data establishes variability; it cannot pass a speed comparison. Tail claims need the stated sample counts.

configuration.exclusionPolicy: Retain every attempted launch and sample. Unexpected errors invalidate a comparison, not individual slow observations. Only an explicitly documented external interruption can invalidate an entire run. Never rerun selectively.
configuration.executionOrder: Rotate workloads by launch index; paired engine comparisons must alternate which engine starts each launch pair.
configuration.resourceCoverage: External watchdog samples the observed descendant process tree, including separately grouped browser processes. Short-lived processes between samples may be missed; report this limitation.

contenders.selectionPolicy: A declared initial set spanning the compatibility reference, direct Chrome automation, an integrated browser test runner and the WebDriver/BiDi ecosystem. Inclusion does not assert a popularity rank or an unmeasured speed ranking. Expand the set when a relevant faster contender is identified.

competitors.reason: Compatibility reference and established end-to-end runner; existing matched library-flow baseline.
Direct Chrome automation contender with native locator readiness and low-level browser control; useful for testing whether the independent engine beats an automation library as well as a runner.
Integrated end-to-end runner with browser-side command execution and retrying assertions; its event model and runner costs require a separate suite comparison.
WebDriver/BiDi ecosystem contender with native user interactions and standalone or runner execution; record the actual negotiated protocol and browser driver.

admission.policy: Functional admission runs retain observations and elapsed time but do not enter performance tables as comparative measurements. Successful application outcomes, exact request counts, trusted events, fresh-context isolation, launch identity and clean watchdog exit are mandatory. Deviations from the reference operation/event contract must be reported explicitly.

contenders.performancePolicy: Use the independent-launch sampling, exclusion, uncertainty and regression thresholds in baseline.json. Library-flow observations do not stand in for full runner-suite or contention results. No current broad competitor leadership claim.

webdriverio.reason: ChromeDriver owns launch and the BiDi mapper bootstrap page. Retain its native defaults and report the difference from the reference pipe-only/no-startup-window policy. Launch-policy equivalence is not established.
